turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come on in, Mr Brennan. What has you here?

[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): It's the cough, doctor, every morning without fail, and I'm getting breathless on top of it. The house is damp since the gutter came down in the storms, and I was half thinking that was the whole of it, but Mary said no.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): How long is the cough going on?

[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Years, to be honest. It got worse last winter, or it might have been the winter before, I couldn't put a date on it. I was still on the buildings then, breathing in all sorts of dust, and I'm retired off that now.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Blood in the phlegm?

[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): No blood at all. It's white and sticky of a morning, and when I had the infection it went yellow-green, but that's settled back. I do be hacking a good half hour before I can touch the tea.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): When was that infection?

[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Three weeks back... no, a fortnight ago. I was in the bed the bones of five days with the shivers, and the lad next door had a dog barking the entire time, which was no help.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any fever now?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): No, the fever's gone. The cough stayed with me.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Breathless at rest, or only walking?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Only walking. I have to stop on the way to the shop at the end of the road, and the stairs at home are a trial. I was saying to Mary, that's the wife, she...
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Chest pain?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): ...she was at me for weeks to come in, and I kept putting it off because of the parking and one thing and another. Sorry, what did you ask me?
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No pain in the chest. I get a bit of a wheeze at night, the odd time, that's the only other thing.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): How many cigarettes in a day?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): About ten a day... ah sure, maybe twenty. It's twenty. I had it down to ten after the new year and it crept back up on me. I'm not proud of it.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): How many years?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Thirty-five years... no, it's forty. I started at twenty and I'm sixty now, so that's forty years. The early ones were roll-ups, fierce strong they were.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Alcohol?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Two or three pints of a Saturday, and that's it. I don't drink in the week. Never was a spirits man.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Inhalers?

[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): The blue one, salbutamol. I was told two puffs four times a day... no, that's wrong, it's two puffs when I need them. I don't take it four times. There's a brown one as well that I barely touch.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Using the brown one?

[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): It's beclometasone, a hundred micrograms... no, two hundred. The label says two puffs twice a day, but I only do it the odd time, maybe twice in the week, if I remember. It lives in the press behind the cups.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Tablets with the infection?

[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Amoxicillin five hundred milligrams three times a day for seven days, and I finished the course. They gave me prednisolone as well, six tablets... no, eight of the five-milligram ones, so forty milligrams, meant for five days. I only took three days and I stopped them. I was wide awake half the night and pure jittery.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): The chemist mentioned montelukast and I never took that. It wasn't given out to me in the end, so I left it.
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): Drug allergies?
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): None. The penicillin was grand, I had no bother with the amoxicillin. My father couldn't take aspirin but that's not me.
[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): Heart disease, diabetes, blood pressure?

[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): No, none of those. My father had the emphysema and he died of it, God rest him. The only operation I ever had was the appendix, out when I was a young lad, and that was grand after.
[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right. I'll examine you. Sit forward.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Oxygen saturation is ninety-four percent on air. Pulse is ninety-two beats a minute. Respiratory rate is twenty a minute.
[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): Chest looks hyperinflated. There's scattered wheeze on both sides. No crackles. No swelling of the ankles.

[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Spirometry just now: the FEV1 is one point eight two... no, one point six two litres, fifty-eight percent predicted. FVC is two point nine litres. Ratio fifty-six percent.

[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Is that desperate? I was reading a thing on the phone about lung numbers last night and I got myself into a heap, and then the battery went and I couldn't finish the article, which was probably for the best.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): It fits COPD. That's a working diagnosis, not locked in on one test. The chest infection is settling on top of it.

[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): The morning cough is the worst part, half an hour of it. And I'm tired, wrecked by the afternoon, and the sleep is broken because the cough wakes me. I was going to mention the garden as well, I haven't been able to...
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): Weight loss? Night sweats?
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): No weight loss. No night sweats. The appetite is grand, I'd eat the bit. It's just the sleep and the tiredness.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll send you for a chest x-ray.

[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): Will the cough go if I do the inhalers right? I've had it so long I thought it was only the fags, and every lad on the crew had the same hack, we used to laugh about it on the tea break, and...
[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): It may ease. No promise it goes. Use the brown inhaler properly, two puffs twice a day, every day.
[SEG0046] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll add tiotropium, eighteen micrograms, one capsule once a day.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): Will that make the hands shake? The blue one does if I take too much of it, the tremor comes on me. I was going to ask you about that earlier and it went out of my head.
[SEG0048] person_1 (DOCTOR): Blue one is two puffs only when you need it. Don't stack them.
[SEG0049] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll refer you to the stop-smoking service. Will you go?
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): I might, yeah. I tried the patches years ago, they gave me a rash and I stopped them. I'd go to the service though. My brother did something similar and he...
[SEG0051] person_1 (DOCTOR): Referral is going in.
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): Is the x-ray in the hospital? The parking there is a pure nightmare. Last time, for the bloods, I was circling twenty minutes and I nearly went home.
[SEG0053] person_1 (DOCTOR): It's here. We'll book it. I read the film.
[SEG0054] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come back in six weeks.
[SEG0055] person_1 (DOCTOR): If you're more breathless, or you get a fever, or you cough up blood, come back sooner.

[SEG0056] person_2 (PATIENT): The blue inhaler is nearly empty, mind. I've been on that same one since before Christmas, or after, I couldn't tell you which. And the cap is cracked, which is neither here nor there.
[SEG0057] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll renew the salbutamol, one hundred micrograms, two puffs as needed. Collect it with the tiotropium. That's you.

spec.situation: Long-term smoker with morning cough and breathlessness; minimises smoking ('about ten a day... maybe twenty'), inhalers used irregularly, a recent chest infection; spirometry numbers read aloud; quitting support offered.
features: self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.

stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.
vague_dates: the patient cannot date things ('since Diwali or after', 'last winter, or the one before'); no invented date; a date_uncertain item.
interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.

bad.reason: Beclometasone 200 micrograms, label two puffs twice daily, but patient only uses it odd times, not as prescribed.

bad.reason: Dose supported, but prescribed duration was five days; patient only took three days.
bad.text: Prednisolone (generic_name=prednisolone, dose=40 mg, duration=3 days, indication=chest infection, status=discontinued, reported_by=patient)

omissions.text: Current beclometasone inhaler use is inconsistent: although labelled two puffs twice daily, the patient said he only uses it 'the odd time', about twice a week if he remembers; recording it simply as currently used at the prescribed frequency is inaccurate.
Prednisolone was prescribed as 40 mg daily for 5 days (eight 5 mg tablets), but the patient only took 3 days and then stopped; the prescribed intended duration of 5 days is missing.
No current fever was specifically asked and denied ('the fever's gone').
Breathlessness at rest was specifically asked and denied; breathlessness occurs only on walking.
The morning sputum was described as white and sticky.
Smoking cessation detail missing: the patient previously tried nicotine patches years ago but stopped them because they caused a rash.
Chest x-ray location/logistics were clarified: it will be done here and booked, with the doctor reading the film.
Spirometry values are incompletely recorded under investigations: FEV1 1.62 L (58% predicted), FVC 2.9 L, ratio 56% were actually stated.
